title: But First, Coffee
statementMd:
Lois Griffin has hung a new sign in the kitchen: "*But first, coffee.*" Peter finds this deeply illogical, as you can't say something comes "first" without knowing what it's being compared against.

To settle the argument, Peter gathers a line of n people in the kitchen, represented as a string s. Each person either wants coffee (si=C) or is having a life-threatening emergency (si=E).

Lois insists that coffee should always come first, so she wants to rearrange the line so that all C's appear before all E's. Lois can only perform the following operation, any number of times:

— Choose 3 indices 1≤i<j<k≤n and right shift or left shift the values on si, sj, sk cyclically.

For the string CCECCE, if she chooses i=1,j=2,k=3 and performs a right shift cyclically, the string becomes ECCCCE. If she chooses i=4,j=5,k=6 and performs a left shift cyclically instead, the string becomes CCECEC.

Determine the minimum number of operations Lois needs to rearrange s so that all people who want coffee come before all people having emergencies.

## Input

The first line contains n (3≤n≤105) — the length of the string.

The second line contains s, of length n. A character in s will only be either C or E.

## Output

Output a single integer — the minimum number of operations required to sort the given string s.

## Note

In the first sample, `CCE` is already in the required order, so the answer is 0. In the second sample, one cyclic shift using positions 1, 2, and 4 changes `CEEC` into `CCEE`, so one operation is enough.
